sentences.text:
The Petitioner has filed this petition under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation of
Rs.20,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident dated 11.03.2023.
2. The case

of the Petitioner in brief is that, On 11.03.2023 at about 8.15pm when he was traveling in a Two Wheeler bearing Reg.No.KA-05-JD-7281 near Mattihalli Gallarahatti gate, NH-206, Kasaba Hobli, Tiptur Taluk, Tumkuru - Karnataka, a Car bearing Reg.No.KA-02- MS-0795 came rashly and negligently without caring for SCCH - 25 3 MVC No.1737/2023 human safety and dashed against the petitioner.
Due to impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

3. It is the further case of the petitioner that, immediately after the accident he was taken to Tiptur Govt. Hospital for treatment and then shifted to Janapriya Hospital, Hassan for further treatment,
operated to the injuries and discharged with advice.
So far he has spent Rs.3,00,000/- towards medical expenses, conveyance, food and nourishment etc.,
At the time of accident he was hale and healthy, working as a Supervisor and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
Due to accidental injuries he lost his income.
He is put to great hardship and mental agony and shock.
The accident caused due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-02-MS-0795.
The Honnavalli Police have registered a case against the driver of the offending vehicle in Cr.No.20/2023.

Therefore, the 1st respondent being the insurer and the 2nd respondent being the Owner of the said SCCH - 25 4 MVC No.1737/2023 offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to him.
Hence, this petition.
4. In response to notice issued by this Tribunal, the Respondents appeared through their respective counsels and filed separate written statements.
5. The objection of the respondent No.1.
It has denied all the petition averments.
It has denied the issuance of policy in respect of the vehicle bearing No.KA-02- MS-0795.
The driver of the vehicle has no valid and effective DL as on the date of accident.
The petition is also bad for non compliance of Sec.158(6) & 134(c) of MV Act.
The rider of the bike did not have valid and effective DL to ride the vehicle and he was proceeding without helmet.
Further contended that the accident was caused due to the negligent act on the part of the petitioner himself.
It has also denied the age, occupation and the manner of accident.
It contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is excessive, arbitrary and SCCH - 25 5 MVC No.1737/2023 disproportionate.
Therefore, prayed for dismissal of the petition against it.

6. On the above rival contentions of the parties, this court has framed the following issues:-

He has reiterated the contents of the petition in his affidavit filed in lieu of his chief examination.
During his cross examination, nothing worthwhile is elicited.
The Respondent No.1 insurer has contended that there was sole negligence on the part of the petitioner and at the time of accident the petitioner did not weare helmet.
In order to prove their contention they have not SCCH - 25 7 MVC No.1737/2023 examined any witness.

Ex.P.4 shows that the car suffered damages to the front right side bumper, front right side head light and front right side bonnet and ventilation grill, whereas the motorcycle suffered damages to the front wheel mudguard assembly,
both indicators, front registration number plate, front left side handle grip and front left side crash guard.
Ex . P.5
Sketch shows the place of the accident.
To the notice given under Ex.P.3, the owner of the Car has replied.

12. Issue No.2:-
In order to prove the injuries and disability suffered by the petitioner, the petitioner has produced the wound certificate as per Ex.P.7.

As per Ex.P.7, the Petitioner has sustained Tenderness and swelling and deformity over the right mid 1/3rd of right leg which is grievous in nature.
13.
The petitioner has also got examined Dr.Chidanand K.J.C as PW.2 and got marked Exs.P.14 & 15 clinical notes and X-ray.
He has deposed the details of surgery undergone by the petitioner and diagnosed right leg open type 2 fracture both bones leg.
He further stated that the petitioner is suffering disability from lower limb to the whole body at 14%.
14. PW.2 in his cross examination has stated that he has not treated the petitioner.
The petitioner is young in his 30s.
The healing power is normal at the age.
Fractures are united.
The petitioner can do his Supervisory Job with some SCCH - 25 9 MVC No.1737/2023 difficulties.
The difficulties in doing Co-Ordinate activities may or may not improve with time.
The ROM are interlinked with stability components.
The improvement in ROM there will be improvement in stability and disability may decrease.

Disability:
15.
From the evidence of PW.2 and the documents on record, it is clear that the petitioner has suffered right leg open type 2 fracture both bones.
So it will be difficult for him to sit and walk.
He has stated that he was working as a Supervisor.
This means that either he has to sit, stand or walk for a long time.
This kind of disability will affect his day to day work.
Therefore, this court deems it fit to fix the functional disability at 14%.

Monthly income:
16.
The Petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, he was working as a Supervisor and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
In this regard he has not examined any witness nor produced any documents like Bank statement etc., to prove SCCH - 25 10 MVC No.1737/2023 his earnings.
The accident occurred in the year 2023.
Therefore, this court deems it fit to fix the notional income at Rs.16,000/- per month.
At the time of accident the Petitioner was aged about 34 years as could be made out from Ex.P.11/Aadhar Card as well as Affidavit.
He was hale and healthy before the accident.

Keeping all the above things in mind, Petitioner is entitled to the following compensation:-

sentences.text: After the accident, the Petitioner was treated at Tiptur Govt. Hospital and then shifted to Janapriya Hospital, Hassan, wherein he was treated and was diagnosed which can be made out from Ex.P.8.
Considering that the nature of injury he has undergone is grievous, the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.60,000/- under this head.
ii) MEDICAL EXPENSES:

The Petitioner has pleaded that he has spent a sum of Rs.3,00,000/- towards treatment, medicines,
conveyance, food SCCH - 25 11 MVC No.1737/2023 and nourishment and other incidental expenses etc.
In this regard, he has produced medical bills as per Ex.P.9 for a sum of Rs.1,09,940/- There is no contrary evidence against these bills from the Respondents.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for the above said amount under this head.

iii) LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:-
As mentioned above the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
The petitioner has produced discharge summary of Govt. Hospital, Tiptur to show the details of treatment in the said hospital.
Therefore, considering the nature of injuries it can be said that the Petitioner may have required at least One month time for recovering from the injuries sustained by him.
Hence, he is entitled only for a sum of Rs.16,000/- under this head.

iv) LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME:-
On perusal of Ex.P.11 as well as Affidavit, the petitioner's age is mentioned as 34 years.
Therefore, as on the date of the accident the Petitioner's age is 34 years.
As per the dictum laid SCCH - 25 12 MVC No.1737/2023 down in Sarala Verma's case the appropriate multiplier applicable to his age is 16.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.4,30,080/- (Rs.16,000/- x 12 x 16 x 14%= Rs.4,30,080/-) under this head.
(v) LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND  HAPPINESS:-
The Petitioner was aged about 34 years at the time of accident.

He has sustained grievous injuries and as per consideration of this Tribunal, he is suffering from 14%
functional disability.
The Petitioner has to suffer this disability throughout his life.
Because of this he will have to lose some of the amenities and comforts.

Therefore,
considering the age and nature of injuries that the Petitioner has suffered, a sum of Rs.20,000/- is awarded under this head.
(vi) ATTENDANT, CONVEYANCE, FOOD AND NOURISHMENT CHARGES:
After the accident, the Petitioner was treated in the above said hospitals, admitted as an inpatient and discharged with advise.

However, they have not proved their SCCH - 25 14 MVC No.1737/2023 defence as discussed above.
Therefore, the Respondents being the insurer and the owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
However, as the policy existed as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1/insurer has to indemnify the respondent No.2/insured and has to pay compensation awarded to the petitioner.
The Petitioner has claimed for a sum of Rs.20,00,000/- but he is entitled only for a sum of Rs.6,56,100/- with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.

the petition needs to be allowed.
